title: IN YOUR STORE
description: At left a 56px sentence says Gentrit Rashiti builds the phone and web apps that shoppers, readers and care teams use, above a wheel of four store apps with a red band on Viva Fresh; in the middle are two public store frames of that app and at right two working codes (App Store, Google Play) with the exact URLs under them. Move the band and the frames slide, the facts change and the codes rewrite only the squares that differ; on a phone the codes become store buttons and one frame sits under the wheel.
signature: Big Shoulders Display 800 for the claim (56px), the wheel (40px) and headings, Public Sans text at 17px, JetBrains Mono 14px for years and URLs; paper and ink tinted toward red, with the colour of the selected app (Viva Fresh red, Dukagjini red, Bayyinah maroon, Read to Feed blue, all sampled from the app's own store frame) marking only the selected band and the focus ring; one story moment: the codes write themselves from the centre outwards in 700 ms (expo-out), then spring.snap (600/40) on the band and a 320 ms rewrite of the squares that differ.
rule: The page is a launcher that turns each shipped app into a code your phone can scan.
designRead: Reading this as: a frontend and mobile developer for hiring managers and founders who want shipped phone apps, leading with Viva Fresh (live in both stores), in the rule of a launcher: every public app on the page is a working code that opens it in the visitor's own store.
hook: The one with the wheel of apps and the codes you scan to open the real app in your store.
lead: Viva Fresh: public in both stores, so the proof opens in two taps; its red store frames set the page colour. Read to Feed has the longer record (about 14 releases) but its listings are removed, so it is the fourth row with archived copies.
composition: first-screen.md #6, one mechanism the visitor operates: claim and wheel at left, two real store frames in the middle, two codes at right; the four answers are text and need no input. Differs from a hero + screenshot by putting the control (a list with a sliding band) and its output (frames, facts, codes) in one row.

fourAnswers.desktop: Who: Gentrit Rashiti. What: builds phone and web apps (frontend and mobile developer). For whom: shoppers, readers and care teams. Proof: Viva Fresh live in both stores, two codes with the store URLs, two real store frames, years 2021 to 2026 on the wheel.
fourAnswers.phone: Same sentence in four lines; proof is the four named apps with years, the App Store and Google Play buttons for Viva Fresh and one real store frame under them.

holdback: Original and hook, 7 each. A list that drives a stage is a known pattern (the output is new: working codes), and the memory sentence is a practical fact, not a moment; the one authored moment (the code writing itself) plays once at load and on a phone there are no codes at all. Care-platform proof sits below the first screen because the lead is a mobile app.
skillNotes: HELPED. directions.md: the mechanism table with delete tests, the costume list and the 'the page is a ___ that ___' sentence made me write the rule before any layout, and EXISTING.md showed which control patterns were taken (sun, seam, quality menu, scan to basket) so I looked for a new output instead. motion.md: the build order (end state, cause, token, interruptible, keyboard, reduced) and the tokens worked verbatim: spring.snap 600/40 with velocity hand-off, expo-out for the write-on, 150 ms underline, 'keyboard never animates' became a key-versus-pointer branch, 'multiply by dt' became performance.now. first-screen.md: the four answers and the phone rules ('work above 500px', 'design it, do not shrink it') forced a separate phone layout (wheel above the frame, codes replaced by store buttons). writing.md's translation table (component to building block, query to database request) fixed copy fast. The checker found real defects: C05 hard-failed on 'CV' (a 17px-wide link) and CLS 0.098 on the phone came only from the font swap; T10b caught 'Built with React Native' and T45 caught '21,000' versus '21k' in CONTENT.md. The mid-round checker upgrade fixed my first complaint (canvas counted as work; now only inside data-work, and 'Work counted' lines show what was counted). UNCLEAR OR WRONG. (1) press-and-hover.css puts the grow-in underline at background-position 0 100% and only inside (hover: hover): on a 44px-tall inline-flex link (the target rule) the line sits 15px below the text, and on touch in-text links have no underline at all. I used calc(50% + 0.72em) with background-origin content-box and an underline at rest for links in text, grow-in only for the masthead; the snippet should say so. (2) visual.md says 'metric-matched fallback' but gives no recipe: I measured the width ratio of the real face over Arial with canvas.measureText and set size-adjust, ascent-override, descent-override; measuring mixed text gave 74% and flipped the claim from 5 lines to 4 (CLS 0.009), measuring the claim string alone (77.5%) gave CLS 0. A snippet and the 'measure the claim itself' warning would save an hour. (3) Short link words ('CV', 'Work') need padding to be 44px wide; the skill states height only. (4) --frames counts from navigation start: on an SPA with a lazy route the 150 and 400 ms frames are the host app's loader, and a moment that starts after fonts.ready lands in the 900 ms frame only; a --frames-after <selector> option (or a window.__storyStart marker) would make mid-frames useful. I captured my own series with Playwright. (5) Budget must be checked on a production build: the dev server gave LCP 1.5 to 1.8 s at 4x throttle (C17 warning, jsxDEV alone 70 ms of scripting) while a vite build served from a temp outDir gave 0.64 to 0.76 s with no findings; say so in motion.md step 6 and give the command. (6) 'If original or hook is 7 or less go back to direct' cannot be tested before building, and builders over-score; I scored 7/7 honestly and stayed, which the skill reads as 'park it'. A pre-build test (write the memory sentence, then ask which EXISTING line it could also describe) would be more useful. Also unclear when a control pattern (a list that drives a stage, like hybrid) counts as a different draft from the existing one; the divergence rules talk about skeletons and rules, not controls. (7) M06 (wheel moved the page 1520 of 4394 px) fired once on a phone run and never again, and I could not reproduce it by hand; flaky. (8) T07 flagged a footer link because a grid stretched the underline-gradient link past 60,000 px2; the fix is justify-self: start, but the skill's own underline recipe uses the same gradient. MISSING. An accessible pattern for visitor-driven selectors (radio group with visually hidden inputs, pointer capture only after 5 px so clicks still work, click suppression after a drag, rubber band at the ends, touch-action) and a one-page 'mechanism spec' (pointer, touch, keyboard, interrupt, reduced motion, delete test) would shorten Bold builds a lot. For M3 ('the technique is real') add: prove it with an independent tool; I compared my QR matrices with the qrcode library (56 of 56 identical) and decoded screenshots of the live page with ZXing at 1x and 2x. No guidance on what counts as 'work' when the hook is a generated artefact (a code): I kept it out of the work share and let the real store frames carry 30 percent.
